chunks: Ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Yunus! Whoever withholds the right of a believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will make him stand on the Day of Judgment for five hundred years upon his feet until his sweat or blood flows, and a caller will call out from the presence of Allah: “This is the unjust one who withheld from Allah his right.” He (peace be upon him) said: “So he will be rebuked for forty days, then he will be commanded to be taken to the Fire.”'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for withholding a believer's right according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the severity of withholding a believer's due right, describing a unique eschatological punishment where the offender stands for five hundred years, weeping or bleeding, while a divine caller publicly identifies them as the oppressor. This public rebuke for forty days precedes their entry into Hellfire, highlighting the social and spiritual weight of injustice in Shia jurisprudence. The narration underscores the concept of 'Haqq al-Mu'min' (the right of the believer), linking personal accountability to communal justice.
